examples.en: The wait was long, so I was a little disappointed.
The movie I'd been looking forward to was dull, so I was disappointed.
I was very disappointed when I saw my test results.
My friend forgot our plan, so I was a little disappointed.

examples.ko: 실망하지 마세요. 다음에는 더 잘할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Don't be disappointed. You'll do better next time.

explain: 일에는 에, 사람에게는 에게를 써요. 결과에 실망했어요 / 친구에게 실망했어요.
explain_en: Use 에 for a thing and 에게 for a person. 결과에 실망했어요 (I was disappointed by the result) / 친구에게 실망했어요 (I was disappointed in my friend).

examples.en: The food was really satisfying, and the price was fine too.
This trip was as satisfying as I'd hoped.
The hotel service was very satisfying.
The result wasn't satisfactory, so I did it again.
It was a satisfying meal. I really enjoyed it.

explain: ‘~가 만족스럽다’는 물건이나 일이 주어이고, ‘~에 만족하다’는 내가 주어예요. 서비스가 만족스러워요 / 서비스에 만족해요.

dict_examples.en: I am very satisfied with the result.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 어떤 의무에도 얽매이지 않은 채 기분 내키는 대로 살 수 있는 이곡리 생활이 여간만 만족스러운 게 아니었다.
dict_examples.en: He was extremely pleased with life in Igok-ri, where he could live as he pleased without being bound by any duty.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그 말이 만족스러웠던지 나그네는 껄껄 소리를 내어 웃었다.
dict_examples.en: Apparently satisfied with those words, the traveler laughed heartily.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: With 만족스럽다 the thing is the subject; with 만족하다 you are the subject. 서비스가 만족스러워요 / 서비스에 만족해요.

examples.en: The waiting time was a little unsatisfactory.

examples.ko: 새로 산 노트북 성능이 불만족스러워서 환불했어요.
examples.en: I wasn't happy with the performance of my new laptop, so I got a refund.
The food was tasty, but the portion was unsatisfying.
If the explanation isn't satisfactory, you can ask again.
The delivery speed was unsatisfactory, so I left a review.

explain: 불만족스럽다는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. 말할 때는 “마음에 안 들어요”나 “별로예요”를 더 자주 써요.

dict_examples.en: I am dissatisfied with the reality I'm in.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: His explanation was unsatisfactory to me.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이번 수정안도 불만족스러운 데가 없지는 않으나 이전 것보다는 낫다.
dict_examples.en: This revision isn't without unsatisfactory parts either, but it's better than the previous one.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 불만족스럽다 sounds somewhat stiff. In everyday talk, people more often say “마음에 안 들어요” or “별로예요.”

examples.ko: 후기를 보면 기다리는 시간에 불만족을 느낀 손님이 많았어요.
examples.en: According to the reviews, many customers felt dissatisfied with the waiting time.

examples.ko: 고객 불만족의 가장 큰 이유는 느린 배송이었어요.
examples.en: The biggest reason for customer dissatisfaction was slow delivery.
I told the staff about my dissatisfaction with the service.
That decision brought about dissatisfaction among the staff.

examples.ko: 작은 불만족이 쌓이면 큰 불만이 돼요.
examples.en: When small dissatisfactions pile up, they become big complaints.

explain: 불만족은 ‘만족하지 못한 상태’예요. 불만은 마음에 쌓인 ‘불평’에 더 가까워요. 일상에서는 불만을 더 많이 써요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 불만족 is the state of not being satisfied. 불만 is closer to a complaint that builds up inside you. In daily life, 불만 is used more.

examples.ko: 상을 받은 어린이가 짧은 소감을 말했어요.
examples.en: The child who won the prize gave a short speech about how they felt.
How does it feel after your first day at work?
Please say a word about how it feels to win.
I told my friends how I felt about the trip.

examples.ko: 졸업 소감을 짧게 써서 학교에 냈어요.
examples.en: I wrote a short note about my graduation and handed it in to the school.

explain: 소감은 직접 해 본 일에 대한 느낌이에요. 후기는 그 경험을 글로 남긴 이야기에 더 가까워요.
explain_en: 소감 is what you felt about something you personally experienced. 후기 is closer to a written account of that experience.

examples.en: Watching movies is my hobby.

examples.ko: 영화를 보고 나서 친구와 감상을 나눴어요.
examples.en: After the movie, my friend and I shared our thoughts on it.

examples.ko: 그림 감상에는 설명을 먼저 듣는 것이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Listening to an explanation first helps when you appreciate paintings.
After work I listen to music at home.

examples.ko: 책을 다 읽고 나서 감상을 짧게 적었어요.
examples.en: After finishing the book, I jotted down my impressions briefly.

explain: 감상은 그림, 음악, 영화를 천천히 즐기며 보고 듣는 일이에요. 취미를 물으면 “영화 감상, 음악 감상”이라고 많이 대답해요.
explain_en: 감상 is enjoying art, music or film slowly. When asked about hobbies, many people answer “영화 감상” or “음악 감상.”

examples.en: The teacher showed us a model answer.

examples.ko: 형은 늘 동생들에게 좋은 모범이 돼요.
examples.en: My older brother always sets a good example for the younger kids.
My younger sibling was chosen as a model student at school.

examples.ko: 저는 선배의 일하는 모습을 모범으로 삼고 있어요.
examples.en: I take how my senior colleague works as my model.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 친절한 서비스의 모범 사례예요.
examples.en: That shop is a model case of friendly service.

explain: 모범은 학생, 답안, 사원처럼 다른 말 앞에 자주 붙어요. 서울의 ‘모범택시’는 서비스가 좋은 택시예요.
explain_en: 모범 often attaches in front of other words, like 모범 학생, 모범 답안, 모범 사원. In Seoul, a 모범택시 is a deluxe taxi with better service.

examples.ko: 동생의 그림이 학교 대회에서 우수 작품으로 뽑혔어요.
examples.en: My little sibling's drawing was chosen as an outstanding work at the school contest.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 품질이 우수해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This product is popular because its quality is excellent.
I won an excellence award at the presentation contest.
I was chosen as an outstanding employee and got a gift certificate.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 우수 인재를 뽑으려고 해요.
examples.en: This company wants to hire outstanding talent.

explain: 우수하다는 격식 있는 말이에요. 말할 때는 “잘해요”가 더 자연스러워요. 상, 성적표, 발표에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 우수하다 is a formal word. In speech, “잘해요” is more natural. You'll see it a lot on awards, report cards and in presentations.

examples.en: Congratulations on finishing the picture! It's really great.

examples.ko: 보고서 완성 전에는 퇴근할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't leave work before the report is finished.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 완성이 아니라 아직 밑그림이에요.
examples.en: This picture isn't finished yet; it's still a sketch.
Only one piece is left until the puzzle is complete.
The report is due to be completed next Friday.

explain: 완성은 만드는 일이 다 끝났다는 뜻이에요. 반대말은 미완성이에요. 일이 그냥 끝날 때는 끝나다를 써요.
explain_en: 완성 means the making of something is fully done. The opposite is 미완성 (unfinished). When something simply ends, use 끝나다.

examples.en: Not all the answers were correct.

examples.ko: 올바른 자세로 앉아야 허리가 안 아파요.
examples.en: You have to sit with good posture so your back doesn't hurt.
You have to wash your hands the proper way.

examples.ko: 횡단보도에서 신호를 지키는 것이 올바른 행동이에요.
examples.en: Obeying the signal at a crosswalk is the right thing to do.
I don't know what the right choice is.

explain: 올바르다는 도덕적으로, 예의로 바르다는 느낌이 있어요. 계산이나 답이 맞을 때는 “맞아요”를 써요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: To seek out a proper solution.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He is an upright and sincere person.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 지금까지 부정한 재물을 탐하지 않고 올바르게 살아왔다.
dict_examples.en: He has lived honestly until now, never coveting ill-gotten wealth.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 올바르다 carries a feeling of being morally or properly right. For a correct answer or calculation, just say “맞아요.”

examples.ko: 그저 예쁜 그림이 아니라 따뜻한 그림이었어요.
examples.en: It wasn't just a pretty picture; it was a warm one.
I just wanted to rest quietly.

examples.ko: 그저 궁금해서 물어봤어요. 다른 뜻은 없어요.
examples.en: I asked just because I was curious. I don't mean anything else.
Is he your boyfriend? — No, he's just a friend.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 그저 웃기만 하고 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: He just kept smiling and said nothing.

explain: 그저는 ‘다른 이유 없이’라는 느낌이에요. “~ㄹ 뿐이에요”나 “~기만 하다”와 자주 같이 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 좋지도 나쁘지도 않고 별로 특별하지 않다
phrases.nuance_en: neither good nor bad, nothing very special

explain_en: 그저 carries the feeling of “for no other reason.” It often goes together with “~ㄹ 뿐이에요” or “~기만 하다.”

examples.en: The fruit served at the end was sweet.

examples.ko: 빵집 앞을 지나는데 달콤한 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: As I passed the bakery, I caught a sweet smell.
After I added honey, the tea became sweet.
Eating a sweet dessert puts me in a good mood.
The chocolate is so sweet that I keep eating it.

explain: 달콤하다는 기분 좋은 단맛이에요. 맛뿐 아니라 목소리, 말, 사랑 이야기에도 써요. 그냥 단맛은 달다예요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Apples are both sour and sweet.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 입술이 파래지도록 시큼하면서도 달콤한 찔레 순을 벗겨 먹었었다.
dict_examples.en: We used to peel and eat sour-sweet wild rose shoots until our lips turned blue.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 밤 열두 시의 치킨은 정말 달콤한 유혹이에요.
dict_examples.en: Chicken at midnight is a really sweet temptation.

explain_en: 달콤하다 is a pleasant sweetness. It is used not only for taste but also for voices, words and love stories. Plain sweetness is 달다.

examples.en: I like spicy food as much as my younger brother does.
I practice as often as my friend does.
I can't sing as well as my friend.
My younger brother is as tall as his friend.

examples.ko: 친구만큼 저를 잘 아는 사람은 없어요.
examples.en: Nobody knows me as well as a friend does.
I want to work as hard as my friend does too.

explain: ‘만큼’은 ‘~와 같은 정도’예요. 명사에는 붙여 쓰고(친구만큼), 동사 뒤에는 띄어 써요(먹을 만큼). ‘~만큼 ~는 없어요’는 ‘~가 제일이에요’라는 뜻이에요.
explain_en: 만큼 means 'as much as / to the same degree'. Attach it to nouns (친구만큼) but write it apart after verbs (먹을 만큼). ~만큼 ~는 없어요 means 'nothing beats ~'.
